summary: Rajat Verma works in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
Rajeev Kinra is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (1999–2008) and became an Associate Professor at Northwestern University in 2007.

Rajeev Kumar specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at M. J. P. Rohilkhand University and Panjab University (PhD 2013), later serving as a Panjab University fellow and Assistant Professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).

Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology. After studying at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania, he held posts at IIT Kanpur, IIT (BHU) Varanasi, and IIIT Hyderabad, serving there as Professor from 2002 to 2013.

Indologist Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) studied at the University of Dhaka, completing his doctorate under Sushil Kumar De. He taught at Jagannath University, the University of Dhaka (1939–1951), and Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendrakumar Dabee works in philosophy and Indology. He earned degrees from institutions including the Mauritius Institute of Education, University of Mauritius, Bharathidasan University, and University of Madras, and held posts at the Ministry of Education and Mahatma Gandhi Institute.

Indologist and historian Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) studied at Calcutta Medical College and the University of Calcutta. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and directed the Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

Rajesh P. N. Rao (born 1970) works in computational fields and Indology. He studied at Angelo State University and the University of Rochester under Dana H. Ballard, and became a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington in 2000.

Historian Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University (~1864–1868). He subsequently held posts at Presidency University (~1869–1872) and Scottish Church College.

Raju Rimal works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, and the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (PhD 2015–2019), and held researcher posts at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences.

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he studied under John Marshall, worked at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926), and held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche was a scholar who pursued his studies under Trijang Rinpoche and Gendun Chopel (~1946–1951).

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer (born 1971) studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson. Around 2004, he served as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and as Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, Princeton, and the University of California, Santa Cruz (Associate Professor 1968, Professor 1980), working in philosophy and other fields.
Philosopher Ralph Lerner (born 1928) studied at the University of Chicago under Leo Strauss from ~1947 to 1953. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Chicago from ~1953 to 2003.

Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) studied at Cambridge under Edward James Rapson. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922) and served as Director of SOAS University of London (1922–1957) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1849), Headmaster of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (1854), and Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1861–1878).
Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882) was a philosopher. He completed his studies at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1817–1821), followed by studies at Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).

Raluwe Padmasiri specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He became a Professor at the University of Kelaniya in 2012 and is attested as a Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Ram Chandra Dhungana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).
